# Skeleton

> Grey shapes where content is about to be, so the page doesn't jump when it arrives. A line of text, a circle or a block.

## Install

It lands in `src/rost/skeleton/`, with what it needs and its contract. In an app that uses shadcn:

```sh
npx shadcn add https://rost.build/r/skeleton.json
```

Then import `src/rost/fonts.css` and `src/rost/tokens.css` once, at the root of the app. More on this in [Install](../INSTALL.md).

| `height` | string |  |  |

## Anatomy

- `root`: A `<span>`, hidden from screen readers. Whatever holds the skeletons says it's loading (`aria-busy`).

## When to use

- **Content on its way.** A list, a card or a table whose shape you know before its data arrives. Draw the shape, then swap it.

## When not to use

- **Long waits.** Anything that takes more than a few seconds, or where you know how far along it is. That's **Progress**.
- **Buttons.** A button that's working on something keeps its place and says so itself.

## Behaviour

Plain grey shapes, matched to what's coming: give text lines uneven widths, the last one shorter. They fade slowly between full and 48%, and back, every 1.8 seconds. For someone who asks for less motion they stay still.

## Accessibility

- **Element**: A `<span aria-hidden="true">`. Screen readers skip them.
- **Name**: None. Put `aria-busy="true"` on the part of the page that's loading, and take it off when the content is in.
- **Colour**: Decoration, so no contrast minimum. It's the tertiary grey, which shows on the page and on a card.
